## What's new in 0.3.0

- **PowerPoint files open on any computer, with their click animations.** Presenter now carries its own LibreOffice, so PPT, PPTX and ODP open without PowerPoint or Keynote. Each page key first shows the next click step of the slide, then turns the page. The slide line shows the steps (for example `1/3 clicks`). Some effects are simpler than in PowerPoint (text that flies in just appears), and fonts or charts can look a little different: check a new deck once before class.
- **Videos and sounds of a PPTX play on the slide**: **▶ Video** next to the slide title, or click the ▶ on the video.
- **My timer From–to**: set class periods by clock time (weekdays, AM/PM); it counts down by itself.
- **Black or white screen**: **B** / **W** (or **.** / **,**). Any key brings the slide back.
- **Screens stay awake** while you project or a timer runs.
- **A deck opens again on the page it showed last** (within 3 hours).
- **Marks stay with their slide** while the deck is open. **📷** saves the slide with its marks as a picture.
- **Zoom tool** (Z): drag a box to enlarge a part of the slide. **Whiteboard**: blank pages to draw on.
- **Type a slide number and press Enter** to jump to it. **Name picker** can make random groups.
- **Larger download**: the Windows zip is about 267 MB because LibreOffice is inside. Mac now has two zips, for Apple silicon and for Intel.

## What's new in 0.2.1

- **Class timer**: type the time in **Set** (minutes : seconds); the one **Start** starts it.
- **Warning bells**: up to 5 bells, each with its own time and number of beeps. Open them with **🔔** next to the class timer's name.
- **Change the time**: **±** on either timer adds time to a running timer or takes time away; after the class timer rang, **+** makes it run again.
- **Open deck** starts in the folder of the deck you opened last.

## What's new in 0.2.0

- **Light or dark look**: ☀ / ☾ in the top bar. The console has a new, rounder design.
- **Class timer**: set minutes **:** seconds; warning beeps before the end, and once a second in the last 5 seconds.
- **Marks**: a new **Arrow** tool (A). Hold **Shift** for a straight line, a square box, or an arrow in 45° steps. **Ctrl+Z** (⌘Z) and **Esc** work wherever you draw, also on a program window.
- **Text size** moves 5 % a step; hold **A−** or **A+** to go fast.

## Download

Click one file name under **Assets** at the bottom of this page.

| Your computer | Download |
|---|---|
| Windows 10 / 11 | the file ending in **`-win.zip`** |
| Mac with Apple silicon (M1, M2 …), macOS 13 or later | the file ending in **`-mac-arm64.zip`** (Apple menu → **About This Mac** shows **Chip: Apple M…**) |
| Mac with an Intel processor, macOS 13 or later | the file ending in **`-mac-x64.zip`** |

Do not download "Source code". It is for developers only.

## Open

Nothing to install.

**Windows**

1. Right-click the zip → **Extract All**.
2. Open the new folder and double-click **Presenter**.
3. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC": click **More info → Run anyway**. This is needed once.

**Mac**

1. Double-click the zip. You get **Presenter**.
2. Double-click **Presenter**. If macOS says it cannot check the app: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down, click **Open Anyway**. This is needed once.
3. PPT and PPTX files open with the LibreOffice inside Presenter. The Mac version of this has not been tried on a real Mac yet: if a PPT does not open, save it as PDF and tell the maintainer.
4. To show program windows (a browser, a video …), allow Presenter in **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording**, and, when asked, **Accessibility**.
